transcript.text: w/m finally died after 12 yrs, whats the best one to buy under £400? family of 5

I can't offer specific buying advice or recommend models within a budget, as my role is strictly to help diagnose and repair your current appliance. However, given it has lasted 12 years with a family of five, it may be worth checking if the failure is something simple like a blocked filter, a failed door lock, or worn motor brushes before replacing it entirely. If you'd like to try a quick check to see if it can be revived for free, I can guide you through that.
ok, it stopped mid-cycle with water still in the drum, won't drain or spin, just hums. if it's cheap to fix i'd try, what should i check?

That humming sound while water remains usually means the pump is trying to push water out but is blocked or jammed. The most common and cheapest fix is a blockage in the filter or something caught in the pump itself. Please switch off and unplug the machine first for safety. Then, open the small flap at the bottom front to access the drain filter (have a towel ready as water may spill). Tell me: 1) Was the filter clogged with gunk? 2) Once removed, can you see the plastic impeller inside the hole—does it spin freely or is something stuck in it?
didn't know there was a filter tbh. haven't looked yet, will have to do it. water still in the drum so is it just a towel job? model reads WMBF944P on the door rim if you need it

Yes, it will be a bit of a towel job—place plenty of old towels in front of the filter flap and on the floor to catch the water. Once you've opened the flap and unscrewed the filter (it may take a few turns), tell me: 1) Was the filter clogged with gunk or did you find any objects like coins or buttons? 2) With the filter out, can you see the small plastic impeller inside the hole—does it spin freely when you turn it with your finger, or is it jammed?
ok haven't done it yet, will do it now. unplugging first and going slow as there's still water in the drum. will report back

That sounds like a sensible approach—taking your time with the water will keep things tidy. I'll be here when you're ready; just let me know if the filter was blocked and whether the impeller inside spins freely once it's out.
ok, doing it now, back in a few mins

No rush—just make sure you have plenty of towels down to catch that standing water. When you've had a chance to check, let me know if the filter was clogged with gunk or debris, and whether the plastic impeller inside spins freely once the filter is out.
